docs.title: Welcome
docs.text:
Welcome to the documentation of the Super-Computing Center Semantic Structures (SuCCeSS)!

Please find the collected documentation of the generic model for (super)computer centers as developed as part of the creation of a semantic digital twin at CSCS

Get started by having a look at the model and its types

If you have any questions, feel free to reach out by e-mail.

docs.title: Model
docs.text: The model is a definition of entities and relations which we would like to use to describe the center. It is meant to create a semantic digital twin of any larger computation center with focus on HPCs.

docs.title: Dataset
docs.text:
A Dataset is a logical, cataloged data source used for measurement, analytics, or observability purposes. It represents a well-defined stream or collection of data such as a Kafka topic, an Elasticsearch data stream, or a database table. In this context, a Dataset is used to identify, classify, and govern data producers and consumers, track data volume and quality metrics, and support lineage, retention, and access control across data platforms.

Fully qualified name: https://kg.svc.cscs.ch/types/Dataset

Properties

  • description

  • name

Outgoing relations:

  • fields (one or many) of type DatasetField

  • sources (one or many) of type DatasetSource

Incoming relations:

  • has access examples (dataset) of type DatasetAccessExample
  • has responsabilities (relatesTo) of type Responsibility

docs.title: Dataset Access Example
docs.text:
A Dataset Access Example provides a concrete illustration of how a Dataset or Dataset Source can be accessed or queried by consumers. It includes representative access patterns such as a Kafka consumer subscription, an Elasticsearch query, or a SQL statement for a database table. Dataset Access Examples are used in a data catalog to improve discoverability, accelerate adoption by users, and demonstrate correct and efficient usage of the dataset while respecting access controls and governance policies.

Fully qualified name: https://kg.svc.cscs.ch/types/DatasetAccessExample

  • code

  • description

  • name

docs.title: Dataset Field
docs.text:
A Dataset Field represents a single logical attribute or column within a Dataset Source. It defines an individual data element such as a message field in a Kafka topic, a field in an Elasticsearch document, or a column in a database table. Dataset Fields capture metadata including name, data type, semantic meaning, and optional constraints, and are used for schema management, data quality checks, impact analysis, and governance within a data catalog.

Fully qualified name: https://kg.svc.cscs.ch/types/DatasetField

  • description

  • name

Outgoing relations:

Incoming relations:

docs.title: Dataset Field Type
docs.text:
A Dataset Field Type defines the logical and technical data type of a Dataset Field. It describes how field values are structured and interpreted, such as string, integer, floating-point, boolean, timestamp, or complex types like arrays and objects. In a data catalog context, Dataset Field Types enable schema standardization, validation, compatibility checks across systems such as Kafka, Elasticsearch, and relational databases, and support data quality enforcement and lineage analysis.

Fully qualified name: https://kg.svc.cscs.ch/types/DatasetFieldType

docs.title: Dataset Quality Measurement
docs.text:
A Dataset Quality Measurement represents a quantified assessment of the quality of a Dataset or Dataset Source over a defined time period. It captures metrics such as completeness, freshness, validity, consistency, uniqueness, and error rates for data originating from sources like Kafka topics, Elasticsearch data streams, or database tables. Dataset Quality Measurements are used to monitor data reliability, detect anomalies, enforce data quality expectations, and support governance and operational decision-making.

Fully qualified name: https://kg.svc.cscs.ch/types/DatasetQualityMeasurement

Properties

docs.title: Dataset Source
docs.text:
A Dataset Source represents the concrete technical origin of a Dataset within a data platform. It identifies where and how the data is produced or exposed, such as a Kafka topic, an Elasticsearch data stream, or a database table or view. The Dataset Source captures source-specific attributes including platform type, namespace, schema, retention policy, and ingestion method, and is used to support data cataloging, lineage tracking, usage measurement, and governance.

Fully qualified name: https://kg.svc.cscs.ch/types/DatasetSource

docs.title: Dataset Source Field Type
docs.text:
A Dataset Source Field Type defines the concrete, platform-specific data type of a Dataset Source Field as implemented in a particular data system. It describes how the field is physically stored and encoded, such as an Avro type in Kafka, a mapping type in Elasticsearch, or a column type in a relational database. Dataset Source Field Types are used to ensure schema correctness, validate compatibility between producers and consumers, and support data quality, evolution, and lineage tracking across heterogeneous data platforms.

Fully qualified name: https://kg.svc.cscs.ch/types/DatasetSourceFieldType

This grouping supports optimized scheduling, workload isolation, and efficient communication patterns across the HSN fabric.

docs.title: VLAN
docs.text:
A VLAN (Virtual Local Area Network) is a logical network segment used to separate and organize traffic within HPE infrastructures. VLANs allow compute nodes, switches, management interfaces, and storage networks to be isolated or grouped without requiring separate physical cabling. Each VLAN is identified by a numeric ID and often mapped to specific functions such as management, provisioning, storage, or high-speed interconnect traffic. VLAN segmentation improves security, performance, and traffic control within HPE cabinets and data center environments.

VLAN Groups help classify networks according to usage (such as management, storage, provisioning, or tenant traffic) and simplify the assignment of VLANs to switches, interfaces, and compute nodes. Grouping VLANs improves consistency, eases configuration management, and supports structured network segmentation across cabinets, racks, and cluster environments.

docs.title: Virtual Routing and Forwarding (VRF)
docs.text:
A VRF (Virtual Routing and Forwarding) is a network virtualization technology that allows multiple independent routing tables to coexist on the same physical network device. In an HPE environment, VRFs are used to isolate traffic between tenants, environments, or service domains while sharing the same physical switch or router. Each VRF maintains its own IP subnets, routes, and forwarding rules, enabling secure segmentation and flexible multi-tenant architectures.
